questions.q: Which type of bank account is primarily designed for business owners who make multiple transactions every single day and require overdraft facilities?
questions.a: A Current Account. A wrong answer shows confusion with a Savings Account, which is meant for individuals with limited monthly transactions and has restrictions on the number of withdrawals to discourage commercial use.

questions.q: Why does a Fixed Deposit account offer a higher rate of interest compared to a regular Savings account?
questions.a: A Fixed Deposit locks the money in the bank for a predetermined period, allowing the bank to lend that stable pool of funds out for longer terms without fear of sudden withdrawal. A wrong answer reveals the misconception that banks give higher interest just to be generous, ignoring that interest rewards the depositor for giving up immediate access to their liquidity.

questions.q: Rohan deposits ₹10,000 into a Fixed Deposit for 1 year at an annual simple interest rate of 6%. How much total money will Rohan receive when he closes the account at the end of the year?
questions.a: Steps: 1. Identify principal amount ($P = ₹10,000$), rate ($R = 6\%$), and time ($T = 1\text{ year}$). 2. Use simple interest formula: $\text{Interest} = \frac{P \times R \times T}{100}$. 3. Calculate interest: $\frac{10000 \times 6 \times 1}{100} = ₹600$. 4. Calculate total maturity amount: $\text{Principal} + \text{Interest} = 10000 + 600 = ₹10,600$. Answer: ₹10,600. A wrong answer indicates an error in calculating percentages or forgetting to add the interest back to the principal.

questions.q: Analyze the impact if a businessman running a grocery wholesale shop tries to use a standard Savings Account instead of a Current Account for his daily operations.
questions.a: The businessman will likely exceed the bank's monthly limit on free transactions and deposits, attracting heavy penalty fees, and he will be denied business-specific features like overdraft facilities. A wrong answer shows a failure to recognize that personal and business financial needs operate under completely different rules and bank regulations.

questions.q: Evaluate whether a retired person living on a fixed monthly pension should keep all their life savings in a Current Account to ensure they can withdraw cash anytime.
questions.a: This is an inefficient financial choice because a Current Account offers zero interest, meaning inflation will erode the purchasing power of their life savings over time. A better choice would be a combination of a Savings Account for daily expenses and Fixed Deposits or senior citizen schemes for earning steady interest. A wrong answer reveals a misunderstanding of the trade-off between absolute liquidity and earning returns to beat inflation.

questions.q: Propose a financial plan for a 14-year-old student who receives ₹2,000 as a birthday gift and wants to save it for a school laptop purchase two years later, while earning some extra money on it.
questions.a: The student should open a minor Savings Account or a short-term Fixed Deposit/Recurring Deposit tailored for youth to safely store the funds and earn interest over the two-year horizon. A poor answer suggests keeping the cash in a piggy bank at home, ignoring the safety benefits and interest-earning potential of banking infrastructure.
